chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said:

It was said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The people are reporting that Ali (peace be upon him) said upon the pulpit of Kufa: O people! You will be called to insult me, so insult me. Then you will be called to disavow me, so do not disavow me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'How often do the people lie against Ali (peace be upon him).'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'He only said: You will be called to insult me, so insult me. Then you will be called to disavow me, and I am upon the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), but he did not say: Do not disavow me.'

So the questioner said to him (peace be upon him), 'What do you think if he chose death rather than disavowal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! That would not be upon him, and he would have no excuse except what was for 'Ammar ibn Yasir, when the people of Mecca coerced him while his heart was at rest with faith.'
Except the one who is compelled while his heart is at rest with faith.

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him at that time: O 'Ammar! If they return (to coercing you), so return (to saying what you said), for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed your excuse and commanded you to return if they return.

key_terms.عَمَّارُ بْنُ يَاسِر: Ammar ibn Yasir, a companion known for his dissimulation
key_terms.مُطْمَئِنّ: At rest or firm (regarding the heart)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) actually say about being insulted and disavowed, and what is the ruling on dissimulation (taqiyya) in cases of coercion?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the popular narration by clarifying that he affirmed his adherence to the Prophet's religion rather than commanding public disavowal, thereby distinguishing between the act of *taqiyya* and the internal state of faith. He anchors this ruling in the precedent of 'Ammar ibn Yasir, whose heart remained firm during coercion, establishing the principle that external utterance under duress does not negate inner belief. This hadith serves as a foundational text for Shia jurisprudence on *taqiyya*, emphasizing that the preservation of life through dissimulation is a divine concession, as confirmed by the Prophet's instruction to 'Ammar to repeat the act if persecution continued.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa who said,

‘It was said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The people are reporting that Ali<sup>asws</sup> said upon the Pulpit of Al-Kufa: ‘O you people! You will be called to insulting me<sup>asws</sup>, so insult me<sup>asws</sup>. Then you would be called to denounce me<sup>asws</sup>, but you will not denounce me<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How frequently the people lie against Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘You would be called to insult me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, so insult me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, then you would be called to the disavowment from me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, and I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> am upon the Religion of Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, but he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> did not say: ‘Do not disavow from me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’.

So the questioner said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘What is your view if I choose being killed instead of disavowment?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! That would not be upon him, and what would be for him except what Ammar Bin Yasir passed upon where the people of Makkah coerced him, and his heart was at rest with the Eman?
So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Revealed with regards to it [16:106] except the one who is compelled while his heart is at rest on account of faith.

So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said to him during it: ‘O Ammar! If they were to repeat (coercing you), so repeat (what you said before), for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Revealed and Excused you, and Commanded you to repeat if they were to repeat (coeercing you)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqa who has said the following:

“It was said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘People narrate that Ali (a.s.) once said from the pulpit in al-Kufah, “O people, one day you will be told to abuse me. You then will do so, then you will be told to denounce me but you will not denounce me.” The Imam said, ‘How often has this falsehood (lie) been told about Ali, recipient of divine supreme covenant.’

The Imam then said, ‘What he said was: ‘One day you will be told to abuse me, you must do so then you will be told to denounce me, and I follow the religion of Muhammad, recipient of divine supreme covenant. He did not say do not denounce me.’

The person asking the question then asked, ‘Do you say he must have chosen being murdered instead of denouncing?’ The Imam said, ‘By Allah, there was no such thing necessary for him to do. There was nothing for him but that which happened to ‘Ammar ibn Yasir when people of Makkah forced him and his heart was confident with belief.
Then Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, revealed His words about it, ‘. . . except those who are forced but their heart is confident with belief,’ ( 16 : 106 )

to which the Holy Prophet said, ‘O ‘Ammar, if they would do such things again you also may do as you have already done; Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has revealed His words about your good excuse and has commanded you to do again what you did before if they ever repeated their misdeed.’”
